Let \(\underline{E}\) be a locally free \(\underline{A}\)-Module of finite rank \(n\). There exists a torsor \(\underline{P}\) under \(\underline{\GL}(n,\underline{A})\) such that \(\underline{E}=\underline{P}\times_{\underline{\GL}(n,\underline{A})} (\underline{A})^n\), where \((\underline{A})^n\) is regarded as a \(\underline{\GL}(n,\underline{A})\)-Module by the standard representation. We can then define a \(\lambda\)-homomorphism from \(R_{\mathbb Z}(\underline{\underline{\operatorname{Gl}}}(n))\) to \(K\) by associating to every representation \(\rho\) of \(\underline{\underline{\operatorname{Gl}}}(n)\) in a free \(\mathbb Z\)-module of rank \(p\) the class of the locally free \(\underline{A}\)-Module
\(\underline{P}\times_{\underline{\GL}(n,\underline{A})} (\underline{A})^p\), where \((\underline{A})^p\) is regarded as a \(\underline{\GL}(n,\underline{A})\)-module by the representation \(\rho\). Under this homomorphism, the class of \(\underline{E}\) is therefore the image of the standard representation. To check a polynomial relation among the \(\lambda^i(E)\), it therefore suffices that this relation hold for the standard representation in \(R_{\mathbb Z}(\underline{\underline{\operatorname{Gl}}}(n))\).
